text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Knesset snub clouds French President Jacques Chirac's visit.
- Hebron talks to resume in Eilat tomorrow.
- Two South Lebanon Army militiamen killed by Hizbollah bomb.
- New service offers "kosher" Internet to observant community.

- Israel proposes focusing on the Hebron agreement and putting off the discussion on other interim agreement clauses. Palestinians fear Hebron-first will be Hebron-last. It's important they be convinced the process will continue, says American source.

- Shekel devalued more than two percent against the dollar in the last two working days. Demand for foreign currency explained, among other things, in expectations for a significant lowering of the interest rate.
- Report: The conflict with the Arabs -- the main reason for a lack of democratic foundation in Israeli education.
- Differences of opinion in Israeli delegation between generals and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's advisers. Right-wing protest grows, including in government, on Hebron agreement being drafted.
- Sara Netanyahu sends two cheques to her children's former nanny.
- Israeli army requests emergency budget to "prepare for any situation" following intelligence warnings the chance of war has risen significantly.
- Negotiations on Hebron: All security subjects have been agreed.
